answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce token stake before their actions count, then slash it when independently verified evidence shows coordinated duplicate identities. A Sybil farmer must therefore fund every fake account, not merely mint names, and risks losing the stake if caught; raising the cost limits cheap identity floods without pretending to prove one person per account. A terrace of accounts may pulse with activity, but jade-colored badges or repeated messages are not evidence on their own.
